name: Amount/Measure of Terumah (Shiur Terumah)
notes: The prescribed proportions for giving terumah: generous (1/30), average (1/50), stingy (1/60), and disputes about minimum and maximum amounts

name: Who May Give Terumah (Ha-Torem)
notes: Rules about who is qualified to separate terumah: excludes deaf-mute, imbecile, minor, non-Jew, and others; partial disqualifications for mute, blind, drunk, naked

name: From Which Produce Terumah May Be Taken
notes: Rules prohibiting terumah from one species for another, from incomplete-processed produce for completed, from attached for detached, from new for old, from Israel for outside Israel, etc.

name: Terumah from Kilayim Species (Min b'Mino in Terumah)
notes: Prohibition against giving terumah from one species for another that is kilayim with it; rules about what counts as the same kind for terumah purposes

name: Intentional vs. Unintentional Violation in Terumah
notes: Distinctions between acting intentionally (mezid) versus unintentionally (shogeg) in giving terumah from improper sources, eating terumah, planting on Shabbat, etc.

name: Verbal Designation of Terumah (Tenuat Peh)
notes: Requirements for valid verbal designation of terumah, including that mouth and heart must be in agreement (3:8), and how to designate from within a pile

name: Terumah Given Through an Agent (Shaliach)
notes: Rules about appointing a household member, slave, or worker to give terumah on one's behalf, and annulment of such authorization

name: Giving Terumah from Clean for Unclean Produce
notes: Rules about separating terumah from pure produce for impure produce and vice versa, disputes between Rabbi Eliezer and sages

name: Eating Terumah Unwittingly (Ochel Terumah b'Shogeg)
notes: Obligation to repay value plus one-fifth (chomesh) for unintentional eating of terumah; who pays the principal and who pays the fifth

name: Eating Terumah Intentionally (Ochel Terumah b'Mezid)
notes: One who eats terumah intentionally repays only the principal value, not the added fifth; the repayment remains hullin and the priest may waive it

name: Medumma (Terumah Mixed with Hullin)
notes: Produce that has become forbidden through mixture of terumah falling into hullin; rules of nullification in 100 parts, proportional rendering of subsequent mixtures

name: Nullification of Terumah in 100 Parts (Bitul Terumah)
notes: The rule that terumah is nullified when mixed with 100 parts hullin; disputes about how to count, cross-type nullification, and deliberate addition of hullin

name: Produce That Grows from Terumah Seeds
notes: Status of produce growing from terumah seeds: first growth is terumah, second growth is hullin; distinction between seeds that disintegrate and those that do not

name: Planting Terumah Seeds
notes: Rules about planting terumah seeds: if unwitting may overturn; if intentional must let remain; distinction based on whether seeds disintegrate in soil

name: Uncovered Terumah Liquids (Gilui)
notes: Terumah wine left uncovered must be poured out due to snake-venom concern; also applies to hullin water, wine, and milk left uncovered

name: Flavor/Taste Imparted by Terumah (Noten Taam)
notes: Rules about terumah ingredients (onions, spices, wine) imparting forbidden flavor to hullin mixtures; application of noten ta'am principle to terumah context

name: Pickling Hullin Together with Terumah (Kavush b'Terumah)
notes: Rules about vegetables or olives of hullin pickled together with terumah, whether whole or crushed; prohibited brine resulting from unclean fish

name: Burning Terumah Oil That Must Be Destroyed
notes: Permissibility of using terumah oil that must be burned for lighting in synagogues, study houses, dark alleys, for the sick, and in celebration vs. mourning houses

name: Order of Separating Terumah and Tithes
notes: Bikkurim precedes terumah, terumah precedes maaser rishon, maaser rishon precedes maaser sheni; violation of this order, though a transgression, is post-facto valid

name: Repayment of Eaten Terumah — Same or Different Species
hebrew: פרעון תרומה שנאכלה מין על מינו
notes: Dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva whether one repays terumah with the same kind or with any superior kind; repayment becomes terumah in the priest's possession

name: Priest's Daughter Married to Israelite and Terumah
notes: A daughter of a priest who married an Israelite loses right to eat terumah; if she ate she repays value but not fifth; her adultery penalty differs from ordinary case

name: Discovery of Disqualifying Status After Eating Terumah
hebrew: נודע שהוא בן גרושה כשאכל תרומה
notes: What happens when a priest discovers mid-eating that he was disqualified (son of divorced woman/halutzah, or has blemish); dispute whether to swallow or spit out

name: Doubtful Terumah (Safek Terumah) in Baskets
notes: Cases of doubt as to which basket contains terumah; the remaining basket treated as terumah for challah purposes; liability when one eats from uncertain basket

name: Stage of Processing Required for Terumah Obligation
notes: Whether terumah may be taken from olives for oil before pressing or grapes for wine before treading; rules about completed vs. incomplete processing

name: Terumah Separated by a Levite from His Tithes
notes: Rules about a Levite who gave terumah from tithe that had not yet had terumat maaser separated; validity depends on whether done intentionally or inadvertently

name: Terumah Given by Non-Jew or Samaritan
notes: Status of terumah, tithes, and dedications given by a non-Jew or Samaritan; dispute about fourth-year vineyard law for non-Jews; whether non-Jewish terumah renders medumma

name: Feeding Terumah to Animals
notes: Vetches of terumah may be fed to cattle, wild beasts, and fowl; rules about who may feed terumah to animals based on ownership and hiring arrangements

name: Partners Separating Terumah
notes: Rules when two partners separately take terumah from shared produce; dispute about validity of both or only the first; depends on whether they conferred

name: Stolen Terumah and Its Repayment
notes: One who steals terumah and eats it must pay double at hullin price plus principal; stealing and not eating requires double payment at terumah price

name: Changing Terumah Produce from Its Natural State
notes: Prohibition against changing terumah from its natural state (e.g., dates to honey, grapes to raisins for wine); exceptions only for olives and grapes

name: Fruit Juice of Terumah as Liquid (Michshirin)
notes: Dispute whether fruit juices other than wine and olive oil (e.g., date honey, apple wine) are considered liquids for purposes of terumah and susceptibility to impurity
